check_ip.description: Check whether one IP address is a Tor exit node, against the list the Tor Project rebuilds about every half hour. Use it to score a sign-up, gate a login, flag an order for review or add context to a support ticket. A match comes back with the relays running at the address, when traffic was last confirmed leaving them, and a link to the Tor Project's own ExoneraTor page to put in a ticket. The list covers IPv4, so an IPv6 address is refused with that explanation rather than told it is not Tor. No API key required.

mock_response.summary: 171.25.193.25 is a Tor exit node, used by 1 relay, last confirmed 41 minutes ago.

check_ip.name: check_ip

check_ips.description: Check a batch of IP addresses at once and get them sorted into what they turned out to be. This is the action for a day's sign-ups, a list of addresses from a log, or the senders on a spike of failed logins. Every address is answered individually, and the result also carries a flat list of just the Tor ones and a single true or false for 'was any of this Tor', so a workflow can branch without counting. Duplicates are collapsed and anything that is not an IP address is reported rather than failing the step. Up to 1,000 addresses. No API key required.

list_exits_for_destination.description: Every Tor relay publishes which destinations it will carry traffic to, and most of them will not carry all of it. This lists the exits that are actually allowed to connect to one address and port (your web server on 443, your mail server on 25) which is usually a much smaller list than every exit there is. Use it to block only the exits that could ever reach you, and to see what share of the network that is before you decide to block at all. No API key required.

description: Tell whether an IP address is a Tor exit node, using the list the Tor Project publishes and rebuilds about every half hour. Check one address or a whole batch from your logs, pull the current addresses to keep a firewall or WAF blocklist in step, look up the relays behind an address, and see which exits are even allowed to reach your service before you decide to block anything. Every result carries the Tor Project's own ExoneraTor link, for the ticket where someone disputes a block. No account or API key required.
